title: Holistic A/B Experiment Runner — Tiered exposure, sequential checks, and deterministic rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: Build a first-class A/B experiment runner for model versions that supports tiered exposure schedules (shadow -> micro-canary -> expanded cohorts), sequential statistical checks for early stopping, and deterministic auto-rollback when predefined safety or quality thresholds are violated.

Background: Teams need a single, auditable control plane to run model experiments against production traffic with predictable safety budgets. Current ad-hoc scripts and manual splits create operational risk and slow iteration. This ticket scopes the product and acceptance criteria for the experiment runner and the corresponding Console UX and API surface.

Scope: MVP focuses on experiment configuration, exposure pacing, deterministic checks for latency/regression/toxicity/quality metrics, UI for monitoring and manual override, SDK toggles for server-side routing, and alerting/rollback automation. Excluded: full Bayesian multi-armed bandit exploration and automated model retraining flows (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Teams can create an A/B experiment in Console or via API with a specified baseline model and one or more candidate variants
Experiment config supports a tiered exposure schedule (shadow, 0.1%, 1%, 5%, custom), plus cohort filters
Sequential statistical checks run automatically after each exposure step and produce clear pass/fail decisions and p-values or posterior summaries
Auto-rollback triggers when any guardrail (latency SLO, end-to-end error rate, safety/toxicity sentinel, or primary quality delta) exceeds configured thresholds
Experiment page shows per-step metrics, raw sample examples, and links to drift/toxicity detectors and evaluation harness
API and SDK support for 'dry-run' shadowing of traffic without affecting latency budgets
Playbook pages and audit logs record every exposure change, manual overrides, and automatic rollbacks
technical_design_summary: Controller service will manage experiment lifecycle states and exposure schedules. It will integrate with the routing layer to apply per-request variant selection and with the telemetry pipeline to compute sequential tests. Sequential checks use alpha-spending approach (e.g., O'Brien-Fleming style) to control false positives during repeated looks. Rollback decisions are deterministic and recorded to audit logs. A lightweight Experiment DSL will be introduced in the API for configuration. The service will be feature-flagged and behind RBAC so only authorized users can create/approve high-exposure experiments.
statistical_checks: Primary method: sequential hypothesis test with alpha spending (configurable alpha and spending function)
Secondary/Bulk metrics: Bayesian posterior overlap checks for small-sample evidence
Minimum exposure rule: do not evaluate beyond 1% allocation until N=1000 samples per cohort or explicit override
Multiple-metric policy: configurable per-experiment ranking of metrics and multi-metric gating (all must pass or majority vote)
Power targets: experiment must declare target MDE and desired power; controller warns if impractical at requested exposure schedule
exposure_control: Stages supported: shadow (0% live exposure), micro-canary (0.1%), small-canary (1%), ramp (5-25%) and custom percentage steps
Cohort-aware splits: select cohorts by header, user segment, geo, or hashed user id
Dynamic pacing: controller can pause or slow ramp if system CPU/GPU utilization or queue latency exceeds configured thresholds
Capacity tie-in: exposure scheduling respects Dedicated capacity pools; will defer ramping if no compatible capacity is available
Safety budget: global per-organization safety budget to limit concurrent experiment exposure across products
observability: Experiment detail dashboard with per-variant time series for primary/secondary metrics, latency P95/P99, error rates, and cost-per-token impact
Example sampling: store a configurable percentage of inputs/outputs for human review and reproduceability
Alerting: automatic PagerDuty/sentinels when negative delta or latency regressions breach thresholds; webhook for external analytics
Audit logs: every schedule change (auto or manual) writes to immutable audit trail with user, timestamp, and reason
Export hooks: ability to export experiment data to S3 or BigQuery for offline analysis
api_changes: New endpoint POST /experiments to create an experiment (payload includes baseline, variants, exposure_schedule, metrics, cohort_filters, stop_conditions)
Field: exposure_schedule: list of objects as steps (time_offset or manual_approval, allocation_percent)
Field: stop_conditions: list of named guardrails (latency_p95 > X ms, toxicity_rate delta > Y, primary_metric p-value < 0.01)
GET /experiments/{id}/status returns deterministic decision state and last statistical summary
console_ui: Create flow: guided wizard with recommended schedule templates and automated MDE/power calculator
Experiment page: compact timeline showing applied exposures, decision points, and simple pass/fail badges
Quick actions: pause, advance to next step, force-rollback, and add notes
Permissions: visibility by team, execute by role (owner/reviewer/observer)

notes: Tradeoffs: stricter sequential testing reduces false positives but increases sample needs and slows iteration; provide 'aggressive' template for product experiments and 'conservative' for enterprise customers
Open question: should cost-per-token be part of auto-decision? Proposal: surface as advisory metric initially, not a gating guardrail
Future: integrate with Optimize to recommend quantization/model size vs quality tradeoffs before running experiments
